title: The rail network: infrastructure given, service derived
description: A bus route can be invented with a slider; a railway cannot. So the track enters as measured infrastructure and the decision variable is the service run on it. Journey times come from line geometry priced at a condition class, never from the published timetable — that timetable describes the system being reformed, so feeding it in would fix today's speed restrictions into an answer about tomorrow. Every condition class must therefore declare the commercial speed it was priced at, because the failure mode worth guarding is not 'geometry was used' but 'a speed was claimed the track cannot deliver'.

network.description: What was measured, so a reader can tell how much of the network the model actually saw.

taggedSpeedShare.description: Share of passenger ways carrying a maxspeed tag. The speed model is length-weighted over these; a low share would make the measured line speed an opinion.

branchLineKm.description: Secondary lines, which are what a feeder service can use without competing for capacity.

commuterMainLineKm.description: Magistrala kilometres a commuter service would occupy, measured by walking every served UAT's path back to its county capital and marking main-line edges once. Overlapping paths share a track: twelve communes down one valley need one extra track, not twelve.

medianDetour.description: Median rail path length over straight-line distance between county seats. Below 1 would mean the graph is cutting corners no railway takes.

seats.description: The station-to-seat residual. A halt two kilometres outside the town it names does not serve that town on foot, and pretending otherwise would overstate what rail reaches.

conditions.description: One entry per track condition class. Keyed rather than listed so a reader can diff two classes on the same pair set.

commercialKmh.description: Required, and the point of the schema: a class that did not declare its speed could be priced at any speed at all.
